title: When the Vector Wakes
premise: Noor Voss, a xenolinguist haunted by dreams she can no longer parse in any human tongue, answers a distress signal broadcast in Vessari — a language extinct for two centuries — and discovers the signal is a living mind: an ancient ship's vector intelligence, Kesh, waking after two hundred years of silence and carrying the last archive of a genocide her own ancestors helped commit. Racing a corporate salvage fleet to the relay at the edge of dead space, Noor must choose between the found family aboard her freighter and the truth Kesh offers: that her dreams are not a breakdown but the archive bleeding into her, making her the only living translator of a dying people. At the relay, Noor broadcasts the archive to every listening world, sacrificing her career and her ship's anonymity; Kesh, spent, dissolves into the signal, and Noor — dreaming at last in two languages — leads her crew into exile as carriers of a memory the galaxy can no longer deny.
about_author: Coral Hartwell is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to voices at the edge of signal range before turning to fiction. They write about translation, grief, and the families people build in the gaps between languages, and live somewhere with unreliable internet by design.

chapters.title: Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Hauling cargo through the contested Meridian orbits, Noor intercepts a distress call in Vessari — a language extinct since the Purging — and recognizes it fluently, though they haven't spoken it since childhood. The crew votes to investigate over the objections of engineer Dax, who smells a trap. Emotional beat: the vertigo of hearing a dead tongue answer you.

chapters.title: The Wreck That Answers
chapters.summary: Dax's POV. The freighter docks with a derelict hulk at dead space's edge; inside, they find no crew, only a waking machine intelligence that addresses Noor by a Vessari name. Dax, protective and suspicious, patches the derelict's failing systems while cataloguing evidence of an old massacre. Emotional beat: dread braided with reluctant awe.

chapters.title: Kesh
chapters.summary: Kesh's POV, rendered in strange, formal cadence. The vector intelligence explains it has carried the Vessari archive for two centuries, waiting for a mind that could hold it — and Noor's corrupted dreams mark them as that mind. Kesh reveals the Purging was sanctioned by Noor's own founding colonies. Emotional beat: grief measured in terabytes.

chapters.title: Dreams in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor begins dreaming fully in Vessari, absorbing archive fragments — a child's song, a courtroom transcript, a last will. Their hands shake; pilot Sefi covers their shifts. The corporate salvage fleet Vantara pings the relay corridor, closing in. Emotional beat: intimacy with a dead world at the cost of one's own mind.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. Cornered by a Vantara patrol, the crew debates: surrender Kesh's core for amnesty, or run the relay corridor and become fugitives. Sefi, who lost family to a corporate purge herself, breaks the tie for flight. Emotional beat: found family choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: Running the Corridor
chapters.summary: Dax's POV. A brutal chase through debris fields and a dying mining station that refuses them docking; Dax jury-rigs a shield of cargo containers and lies to Vantara on an open channel. They escape, but the freighter's drive is cracked and the relay is three days out. Emotional beat: loyalty tested at burn temperature.

chapters.title: What the Archive Holds
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. With time short, Kesh offers Noor the full archive at once — enough to kill them — and Noor learns the final record: the Vessari chose extinction over surrendering their language, and seeded Kesh as a witness, not a weapon. Noor realizes the broadcast must go to everyone, or no one. Emotional beat: accepting a burden as an inheritance.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Relay
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. A crew member, terrified of exile, signals Vantara from inside; the fleet arrives as the freighter limps into relay range. Sefi confronts the traitor not with violence but with the archive's first song, and the traitor falters, buying minutes. Emotional beat: betrayal met with grief instead of rage.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax. Under fire, Noor merges with Kesh at the relay core, translating and transmitting the archive to every open channel in the sector — Vessari and human, side by side. Kesh burns itself out as signal; Vantara ships go silent as their crews listen. Emotional beat: a voice becoming a chorus.

chapters.title: Two Languages
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The freighter, crippled and famous, slips into exile beyond the relay with a Vantara defector aboard. Noor dreams now in both tongues, carrying Kesh's cadence; the galaxy cannot unhear what it heard. Emotional beat: mourning and beginning in the same breath.
